# LocalAgentBrowser

> An autonomous web research agent driven by a local language model (LM Studio) and Playwright. Give it an
> objective; it searches the web, reads pages, records findings with their sources and writes a cited report, all
> on your own computer. Built for small models on a CPU (four tested); no GPU, cloud AI or API key needed.

Key facts:

- Install: `pip install localagentbrowser`, then `python -m playwright install chromium`; run `localagentbrowser`.
  Needs Python 3.10 or later and LM Studio running a model (developed with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, 8,192-token context).
- Good goals: questions you would research by reading pages. Facts, lists with conditions, comparisons with a
  recommendation, how-tos, explanations, views from several sources, lookups in official documentation.
- Not yet: anything behind a form, a login or a button. It reads pages only; it does not click, fill in forms or
  sign in, so flight or hotel prices, shopping and booking sites won't work.
- Speed: on a CPU a run takes about 10 to 60 minutes, and a small model sometimes returns thin findings.
- Tested on four models with identical code (1.64, seven tasks, 90 minutes each, CPU only): Qwen2.5-7B finished
  6 of 7, Llama-3.1-8B 7 of 7, Qwen2.5-14B 5 of 7, Qwen2.5-3B 3 of 7; no finished answer filled a gap from the
  model's own knowledge.
- Windows: a launcher with Start-menu and desktop shortcuts (tools/windows/make_shortcuts.ps1) opens the report by
  itself when a run ends. A Windows installer is planned for the next release.
- Honesty by design: rules in code check the model's claims. Findings must be on the page shown. Before finishing,
  each part of the objective is checked against the findings. What was not found is reported as not found, and
  things the pages didn't prove are marked ("not shown in the pages read to be open-source").
- Privacy: searches, written from your objective, go to DuckDuckGo, and pages are read from the web like any browser;
  the objective itself, the model and the report stay on your computer.
- License: MIT.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/SnowFXXX/LocalAgentBrowser/blob/main/README.md): what it does, the four models tested, install, first run, settings, FAQ
- [How it works](https://github.com/SnowFXXX/LocalAgentBrowser/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md): the loop, code layout, the checks that keep a small model on track, performance, limitations
- [Results by kind of task](https://github.com/SnowFXXX/LocalAgentBrowser/blob/main/docs/task-results.md): single runs and the regression suite by version
- [Example reports](https://github.com/SnowFXXX/LocalAgentBrowser/blob/main/docs/examples/README.md): two unedited reports from a test run, with what each got right and wrong
- [Changelog](https://github.com/SnowFXXX/LocalAgentBrowser/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): every version and why it changed
- [Regression history](https://github.com/SnowFXXX/LocalAgentBrowser/blob/main/docs/regression-history.md): each version measured on seven kinds of task
- [Technical paper](https://snowfxxx.github.io/LocalAgentBrowser/paper.html): Verification over Trust; the design, a four-model evaluation and where the measures failed
